prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1382; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a side impact at an intersection involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports neck and back strain and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the loss. Requested the police report and statements from the other driver.

Entry 3: The police report and the other driver both confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and the account of how the crash happened matches what was reported at first notice.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photos and spoke with two witnesses. Both describe the collision in the same way the claimant did, and the photos show damage that is mostly consistent with the described impact.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant by phone. The account of the crash was the same as in the initial report, with no changes in sequence or detail.

Entry 6: Inspected the vehicle with the appraiser. The damage pattern lines up well with a side impact of this type, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or prior claims history.

Entry 7: A neighbor contacted the office and stated the car looked damaged a few weeks before the reported loss. This has been noted and will be followed up, though the neighbor did not provide specifics about what was seen.

Entry 8: Reviewed the medical records. The reported neck and back strain fits the kind and force of the crash, and no earlier injury to the same body areas is on file.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved, with notes showing steady progress at each follow-up visit.

Entry 10: Reviewed the file with the team lead. The neighbor's comment is the only open item; the rest of the information supports the claim as reported, and the file will be updated once the follow-up is complete.
